function: Predicts the future downlink channel (CSI delay 1 to 8 ms) from P=4 past phase-noise-contaminated coefficients, compensating phase noise first, in massive MIMO-OFDM (p. 1-4).
system: Massive MIMO-OFDM downlink: 32-antenna ULA BS, single omni UE antenna, 72 subcarriers at 3.5 GHz, UE 60 or 30 km/h; no RIS (p. 4, Table I).
method: Progressive learning: curriculum from phase-noise compensation to channel prediction; angular-delay multipath filter, Restormer self-attention, multi-span temporal evolution; supervised MSE losses, 10 epochs (p. 2-4).
data_channel: Simulated CDL-C time-varying channels plus Wiener-process phase noise (linewidth 20 or 200); 14000 training and 3000 test samples; no measurements (p. 2, 4, Table I).
test_conditions: 14000 training and 3000 test samples; evaluated at UE 60 or 30 km/h, PN level 20 or 200, CSI delay 1-8 ms; no cross-condition test stated (p. 4).
baselines: Learned: ConvLSTM [4] prediction and 2D-CNN [7] phase-noise compensation; non-learned: outdated PN-affected delayed channel (R_Effect), plus ideal-channel bound (p. 4-5, Table II).
metrics: MSE, MAE, SSIM, cosine similarity; average spectral efficiency with SVD precoding (predicted vs ideal vs PN-affected channel) (p. 4-5, Table II).
complexity: 456.218K trainable parameters and 214.085M FLOPS, versus 343.116K parameters and 538.526M FLOPS for 2D-CNN (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 4, Table I: "Channel Delay Profile: CDL-C (Angle and Delay Spread)", a 3GPP TR 38.901 CDL profile, used to generate the training and test data.
q2_support: p. 4: "with the same dataset and training overhead (ten epochs)"; Table I gives one train/test split (14000/3000). No scenario, band, or site unseen in training is tested.
q3_support: p. 4: "fairly compared with the benchmark PN compensation 2D-CNN in [7] and the benchmark prediction ConvLSTM in [4]" (learned); the PN-affected delayed channel is the non-learned reference (R_Effect, Table II, p. 5).
q4_support: p. 5: "has 456.218K trainable parameters" and "a computational complexity of 214.085M FLOPS", against 343.116K and 538.526M for 2D-CNN.
q5_support: p. 5: "Codes are available at GitHub" with footnote link https://github.com/TeleRagingFires/Progressive; the data themselves are self-generated CDL-C channels.
notes: Area 2: channel prediction with phase-noise compensation as a prerequisite (p. 1-2). q1: CDL-C is a 3GPP TR 38.901 profile, read from Table I (page image); the paper does not name TR 38.901. q3: non-learned reference is the outdated PN-affected channel (R_Effect column), learned baselines are ConvLSTM [4] (prediction) and 2D-CNN [7] (PN compensation). q2 is 0: one dataset split and no unseen condition stated. Tables I-II read from page images.
